An
Architectural
Vision

My architectural vision is around creating places that are designed with intention, crafted with care, and rooted in meaning and social cohesion. Creating developments that embrace eclectic expression, celebrating contrast, creativity, and boldness to spark curiosity and joy. Every development should be deeply human, shaped by how people live, feel, and connect, and always centred around community by fostering inclusion, participation, and shared ownership. Above all, based on the premise of building with permanence in mind. To deliver places that endure physically, culturally, and emotionally, becoming lasting contributors to the fabric of their surroundings.

Callum Thompson
MRICS MSc BSc
Foreword

A Statement of
Architectural Intent

I have created this document to sit alongside my CV as a statement of architectural intent. My CV details my extensive experience in development management and strategic real estate advisory, showcasing my analytical capabilities and proven ability to manage projects and solve complex development and regeneration challenges.

However, my predominantly consultancy-based career has, until now, limited the opportunity to fully express my creative vision and passion for architecture and design. I believe architecture has the power to shape not only our physical world but also our emotions and communities, meaning developers have a fundamental responsibility to create meaningful places that endure for generations.

My vision, built upon the core principles of cohesive design, eclecticism, neuro-design, community orientation, and permanence, aims to produce timeless, emotionally engaging buildings that are unique and inspiring.

While lacking a formal design background, I possess a discerning eye for design and have harnessed the potential of emerging technologies, including AI tools such as Midjourney, to explore and refine creative architectural concepts. The designs in this document should be considered visions at the earliest stage of design development.

My Vision

Five Pillars of
Exceptional Development

1
Curated

Every element of a development should be carefully considered, from the layout of the kitchen to the choice of landscaped flora. My intention is to curate places that speak to an identifiable, cohesive vision, crafted with care and rooted in meaning.

Wholistic
Every element should be crafted with exceptional care, so that the whole development feels intentional rather than assembled.
Quality Craftsmanship
Delivery standards should ensure every material choice and detail is executed with precision and durability.
Sense of Place
Art, signage, lighting and landscaping should create a distinct and identifiable atmosphere that makes each development feel genuinely itself.
Contextual Integration
Designs should respect local heritage, culture and architectural language, ensuring materials and forms harmonise with and strengthen the existing urban fabric.
Flexible & Adaptive
Buildings should be designed for longevity, incorporating modular or multi-functional spaces that can be adapted for a wide variety of future uses by the community.
2
Community Orientated

Every development should dedicate space for new and existing communities to foster a genuine sense of belonging. Designing for stewardship rather than mere occupation means creating environments that encourage social connection, local identity and participation for people of all ages and backgrounds.

Stewardship
Developments should be designed so that occupants feel encouraged and supported to take shared responsibility, fostering pride and ownership through transparency and trust.
Generous Accessibility
Spaces should be designed specifically for all ages, abilities and backgrounds, removing physical, social and psychological barriers to deliver truly exceptional places for public benefit.
Social Connection
Well-designed public space is the heartbeat of the community. Developments should create environments that encourage both formal and informal interaction and togetherness.
Local Identity
The local ecosystem should be celebrated and strengthened by incorporating commercial spaces that prioritise local businesses, makers and cultural institutions.
Safe, Child Friendly & Inclusive
Public spaces should be welcoming and accessible to everyone, with play spaces designed through the eyes of the children who will use them.
3
Eclectic & Distinctive

The best developments celebrate contrast, creativity and boldness to spark inspiration, curiosity and joy. Working unbound by convention, combining old and new, raw and refined, global and local, creates places that tell a story and feel genuinely memorable.

Celebrate Contrast & Diversity
Embracing a mix of styles, materials and influences, using juxtaposition to create visual interest and storytelling that reflects the multifaceted nature of modern communities.
Designed for Discovery
Layered environments that invite exploration through varied scales, textures and hidden moments encourage people to linger, wander and engage.
Expressive Character
Each development should have a distinct personality, achieved through bold colours, expressive forms and collaboration with local artists and creatives.
Break the Mould
Challenging conventional norms by rethinking typologies, layouts and material palettes uses bold imagination to solve problems creatively and create memorable landmarks.
4
Human

Every development should be deeply human, shaped by how people actually live, feel and connect. Neuro-design principles, biophilic integration and generous accessibility from the public realm to the individual bedroom build places where everyone feels seen, safe and inspired.

Neuro-Design
Considering all elements of design to purposefully evoke specific emotional responses, using colour psychology, spatial orientation and contrast between energising and restorative zones.
Accessible for All
Accessibility requirements should be incorporated early in the design process, promoting positive and equal experiences and enabling long-term, adaptable and inclusive living for everyone.
Biophilic Integration
Connecting people with nature through natural materials, considered landscaping, water features and daylight reduces stress and enhances cognitive function and overall wellbeing.
5
Permanent

Developments should stand as testaments to enduring design and quality craftsmanship for generations to come. Designing with future climate resilience in mind, prioritising ambitious sustainability and specifying robust materials ensures structural and environmental longevity.

Future Climate Resilience
Designing for a hotter and more extreme future climate, drawing inspiration from the southern Mediterranean, Northern Africa and the Middle East, where architecture has long addressed the challenges of extreme temperatures.
Built to Last
Robust construction methods and durable materials ensure structural and environmental resilience, reducing whole-life carbon and increasing long-term value.
Ambitiously Sustainable
Incorporating circular economy principles, sustainable energy production and passive environmental design makes the best use of available resources across every project.
Three Design Approaches

Designs for
London Living

Rather than presenting a rigid set of solutions, this section offers a glimpse into a breadth of architectural aspirations from across the world, adapted to a London environment at varying scales. All imagery was created using Midjourney and should be considered mood board concepts at the earliest stage of design development.

Californian Modernism

Defined by its seamless integration of indoor-outdoor living, achieved through open floor plans, large windows, and the use of natural materials like wood, stone, and concrete. Adapting it to London requires balancing its core values with climate considerations, sustainable materials, and private outdoor spaces like courtyards or roof terraces.

The Eames House (Case Study House #8)
External Facade

Clean Modernist Aesthetic

The facade presents a clean, modernist form that blends effortlessly into the London streetscape. Opaque glass blocks allow diffused natural light to enter while preserving privacy, creating a sense of intriguing mystery within.

Courtyard

The Outdoors Within

A small, landscaped courtyard acts as the heart of the home, fostering openness and serenity. The design enhances the connection to nature, creating a tranquil atmosphere central to the Californian ethos.

Kitchen

Natural Light & Function

Clean lines and natural wood cabinetry reflect the Californian Modernist aesthetic. The space feels bright and airy, promoting ease and a strong connection to the outside through considered material choices.

Living Space

Open, Light-Filled Living

Openness and abundant natural light define the living room. Natural materials and simple forms create a calm space accentuated by iconic furniture and large windows offering expansive views of outside space.

Bedroom

A Sanctuary of Calm

A light and airy atmosphere enhanced by natural light and simple, elegant furnishings. Natural materials and a minimalist approach create a calm and restful space that truly functions as a retreat.

Bathroom

Clean Lines, Natural Materials

Clean lines, natural materials and a vintage feel maintain the overall aesthetic. A light colour palette and natural light create spaciousness and serenity, promoting peace and rejuvenation.

Moroccan Riad

Meaning "garden" in Arabic, the Riad centres around a tranquil open-air courtyard creating a private oasis. This historic style could be beautifully adapted to London, offering a unique blend of cultural heritage and modern living, with a tranquil courtyard providing a welcome escape within the urban environment.

Le Riad Monceau
External Facade

Mystery Behind the Threshold

A palette of whites and muted tones allows the building to blend into London surroundings. The Moroccan inspiration is subtly hinted at, with a large statement entrance creating intrigue and a promise of hidden wonders within.

Courtyard

The Soul of the House

The central internal courtyard is a versatile, scalable space, communal area for neighbours in larger developments, or the intimate heart of a home. Tropical planting and mosaic tiling create an urban oasis.

Kitchen

Dramatic Contrasts

A chequerboard floor, dark mahogany cabinetry, and a large arched window that floods the room with natural light. Light walls create openness and calm amidst rich textures and a bold material palette.

Living Space

Rich, Enveloping Warmth

A deeply relaxing space dominated by rich, dark red limewash plaster on the walls and ceiling. A low sectional sofa encourages relaxation, while dark mahogany wood elements add richness and a nod to the Moroccan inspiration.

Bedroom

Terracotta Sanctuary

Dark limewash plaster walls in a warm terracotta hue create a haven of tranquillity. Natural light streams in, highlighting dark mahogany furniture, combining soothing warmth and quiet elegance.

Bathroom

Deep Indigo Retreat

A cool, serene retreat with deep indigo tiled walls and a freestanding bathtub. Dark mahogany shutters allow natural light to filter through, creating privacy while maintaining brightness. Blue tones evoke tranquillity.

Australian Federation Filigree

Immediately recognisable for its ornate and delicate detailing, intricate cast-iron filigree on verandahs, balconies, and gables providing shade and expanding living spaces outdoors. In London, the emphasis on covered verandahs could offer comfortable spaces for relaxation regardless of the weather, complemented by a sophisticated contemporary interior.

Derry House, Neutral Bay
External Facade

Victorian Craftsmanship

Filigree detailing, reminiscent of Victorian-era craftsmanship, ensures seamless integration into established heritage areas in London. Porch areas and balcony verandahs extend living space, enhancing both aesthetics and functionality.

Verandah

Protected Outdoor Living

A verandah chosen as the outdoor element in place of a courtyard, more true to this architectural style. Particularly beneficial in London's unpredictable climate, offering a protected, characterful space for relaxation or dining.

Kitchen

Heritage Meets Contemporary

A successful blend of contemporary and historic elements. Bright and airy, with abundant natural light, natural materials, and a modern chrome island, respecting the building's heritage while offering a stylish feel.

Living Space

Luminous Grand Proportions

Floor-to-ceiling windows allow sunlight to stream into the high-ceilinged space. Bold strokes of contemporary design through furniture and furnishings infuse the room with character and vibrant, stylish energy.

Bedroom

Bright, Airy Retreat

High ceilings and abundant natural light create a bright and airy space. Contemporary furniture and a light colour scheme enhance the calming atmosphere, while a balcony provides ventilation and outdoor connection.

Bathroom

Stained Glass Sanctuary

Bathed in soft light filtering through a stained-glass window, this contemporary bathroom is a sanctuary of serenity. Dark green marble grounds the space while the stained glass adds a unique artistic flair.

To Conclude

A Vision of What
Can Be Built

This document showcases a passion for architecture and interior design, demonstrating the ability to develop cohesive and compelling design solutions through the exploration of three distinct architectural styles: Californian Modernism, Moroccan Riad, and Australian Federation Filigree, and the utilisation of AI tools like Midjourney.

While the AI-generated images have their limitations, they serve as a mood board for initial concept ideation and highlight an ability to synthesise diverse influences and translate them into visually engaging and conceptually sound designs adaptable to a London context at varying scales.

This document demonstrates a commitment to detail, an understanding of neuro-design principles, and a focus on creating timeless, enduring developments, a testament to a creative vision and a dedication to crafting spaces that are both beautiful and meaningful.
